verses.text: 1 Say sg, “It was revealed to me that a band of unseen beings[1] listened in and said, ‘Indeed, we have heard a wondrous Recital[2]
that guides to prudence, so we have come to believe in it, and we will never associate anyone with our Lord.
And that [3] most high is the Grandeur of our Lord—He never took a female companion nor a child.
And thatc our fool used to speak untruthfully about Allah.
And that [4] we thought that humans and unseen beings would never say [5] a lie about Allah.
And thatc certain men among humans used to seek refuge in certain men among the unseen beings, but they only increased them in confusion.
And thatd they thought, as you pl thought, that Allah would never resurrect anyone.
And thatd we sought to reach the heaven and found it filled with stern guards and meteors.
And thatd we used to take up positions to listen in, but whoever listens now finds a meteor in wait for him.
And thatd we do not know whether ill has been desired for those on earth, or if their Lord has desired prudence for them.
And thatd some of us are righteous, but some of us are less than that: we have been following divergent roads.
And that [6] we realized that we cannot thwart Allah on earth, nor can we thwart Him by fleeing.
And thata when we heard the guidance we believed in it, for whoever believes in his Lord fears neither loss nor confusion.
And thata among us are Muslims[7] and among us are those who swerve from justice, so whoever has become Muslim—it is they who have pursued prudence.
But as for those who swerve from justice—they have become firewood for Hell.’”
But had they gone straight on the right mode (of life), We would have given them plenty of water to drink,
so as to test them with it. And whoever disregards the remembrance of his Lord—He [8] will insert him into a mounting punishment.
And (say) that mosques belong to Allah, so do not call upon anyone along with Allah.
And thata when the servant of Allah got up, calling upon Him (in prayers), they almost fell on him in a mass [9].
Say [10], “Indeed, I pray only to my Lord, and I never associate anyone with Him.”
Say sg, “Indeed, I possess for you pl neither harm nor prudence.”
Say sg, “Indeed, no one can protect me from Allah, and I will not find any refuge except with Him.
(I have nothing) except for a proclamation from Allah and His messages, and whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger—for him is the fire of Hell, abiding therein forever.
Only when they see what they are promised, will they then know who has weaker helpers and is fewer in numbers.
Say sg, “I do not know whether what you pl are promised is near, or whether my Lord will extend it for a period.
The Knower of the hidden realm—so He does not disclose His hidden realm to anyone
except to a Messenger of His choosing, for He then dispatches guards before him and behind him,
that He may know [11] that they have compiled and proclaimed the messages of their Lord. But He has encompassed what they have, and has tallied everything by number.”

footnotes.1: The Arabic word used is jinn which are unseen beings that are accountable for their actions.
footnotes.2: The Arabic word used is Qur’an which literally means ‘recital’ or ‘recitation’.
footnotes.3: Qira’at: All except for Ibn ‘Amer, Abu Ja’far, Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “And indeed…”
footnotes.4: Qira’at: All except for Ibn ‘Amer, Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “And indeed…”
footnotes.5: Qira’at: Ya’qub read it as: “…would never attribute a lie to Allah.”
footnotes.6: Qira’at: All except for Ibn ‘Amer, Hafs, Hamza, Al-Kesa’i and Khalaf read it as: “And indeed…”
footnotes.7: The Arabic word used is Muslimoun which means those who willingly submit to God, regardless of which prophet they followed.
footnotes.8: Qira’at: Nafie’, Ibn Kathir, Abu ‘Amr, Ibn ‘Amer and Abu Ja’far read it as: “…We will insert him into…”
footnotes.9: Qira’at: Hisham in one of his narrations read it as: “…in masses.”
footnotes.10: Qira’at: All except for Asem, Hamza and Abu Ja’far read it as: “He said…”
footnotes.11: Qira’at: Roways read it as: “…that it may be known that they have…”
